title: When the FDA Expects Food-Effect Studies: Timing, Design, and Review Precedents
summary: When the FDA expects food-effect studies in drug development, the study design it recommends, waiver criteria, and what review precedents show.
body_markdown:
## When the FDA expects food-effect studies: timing, design, and review precedents


Food can change how much of an oral drug reaches systemic circulation and how fast it gets there. The FDA treats characterizing that change as a core clinical pharmacology deliverable for orally administered products, because the answer feeds directly into dosing instructions, exposure-response interpretation, and the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION section of labeling. This overview sets out when in development the FDA expects a food-effect assessment, the study design it recommends, when a study can be waived, and what actual Drugs@FDA clinical pharmacology reviews show about how these studies are run and how their results land in labeling.


### Why the FDA wants food-effect data


For orally administered drugs, the FDA uses food-effect (FE) studies during new drug development to determine whether food affects exposure, how large and variable that effect is, and which meal types matter[11](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=11)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=36) . The general bioavailability guidance frames food effects on bioavailability as an "essential early goal" of pharmacokinetic characterization, with PK work continuing throughout development[2](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=2) . In practice, a food-effect result answers a labeling question: can the drug be taken with or without food, must it be taken on an empty stomach, or must it be taken with a meal.


The FDA judges the clinical relevance of any food effect using the totality of the clinical data, including exposure-response and PK-PD relationships. If the 90% confidence interval for the fed-versus-fasted comparison does not fall within bioequivalence limits, the sponsor is expected to interpret the clinical significance and propose corresponding label instructions rather than default to a mechanical rule[8](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=8) .


### When in development the FDA expects the study


The recurring theme across guidance and review precedent is *early, and on the right formulation* .


**Early clinical development (Phase 1).** Food-effect and relative bioavailability work belongs in early PK characterization, in Phase 1 or initial clinical studies, not deferred to the NDA[2](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=2) . The FDA advises sponsors to assess the effect of a high-fat meal early in development and to test food effects before the pivotal safety and efficacy trials, so the results can guide dose and administration decisions and inform labeling[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=9)[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=14) . Preliminary assessments can be folded into pilot or first-in-human studies[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=9)[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=14) .


Review precedents bear this out. Fosamprenavir (Lexiva) had a "pivotal, Phase I, single dose" food-effect study in healthy adults covering both the tablet and suspension[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=67) . Tofacitinib modified-release (Xeljanz XR) included a "Food Effect on proposed-commercial formulation" study within its Phase 1 healthy-volunteer program[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=81) . Saxagliptin's definitive food-effect study was run at the 10 mg dose used in the Phase 3 program, on a formulation the FDA described as "almost identical" to the anticipated marketed formulation[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=76)[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=80)[83](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=83) .


**On the to-be-marketed formulation, or formally bridged to it.** A definitive FE study should use the final to-be-marketed oral formulation[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=9)[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=14) . The FDA repeatedly pressed sponsors on this point. For enzalutamide (Xtandi), the agency stated it is preferable to conduct the food-effect study with the to-be-marketed formulation[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=65) . For vismodegib (Erivedge), the FDA asked the sponsor to confirm the food-effect study used the to-be-marketed formulation[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=64)[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=66) . For dalfampridine (Ampyra), prior food-effect studies had used formulations different from the to-be-marketed 10 mg SR product, and the FDA said another food-effect study would have to be conducted if the existing one could not be justified for the final formulation[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=68) . For palonosetron (Aloxi), the FDA said the food effect should be obtained for the to-be-marketed formulation and would accept a Phase 3-related result only if the formulations were sufficiently comparable[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=69) .


Where the pivotal formulation already matched the market image, the study could double as both. For testosterone undecanoate (TLANDO), the to-be-marketed formulation was used in both the pivotal Phase 3 study and the definitive food-effect study[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=72) . When an earlier study used a different formulation, the FDA accepted a **bridging** approach: afatinib (Gilotrif) bridged food-effect information from an earlier study to the final market-image Phase 3 product[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=62) , and topiramate (Qudexy XR) had its definitive food-effect result, generated with an "MD" formulation, bridged to the to-be-marketed formulation[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=73) . Aprepitant (Emend) reviews likewise directed that planned clinical pharmacology studies, including the food effect, be characterized with the proposed market image[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=63) .


The practical sequence that emerges: run a preliminary assessment early, then lock in a definitive study on the final formulation (or bridge to it) before the results are relied on for approval and labeling.


### The standard study design


FDA guidance recommends a consistent template for a definitive food-effect study, and reviews show it applied across therapeutic areas.


**Design.** A randomized, balanced, single-dose, two-treatment (fed versus fasted), two-period crossover[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=29) . A three-way crossover is acceptable when the study is also assessing the bioavailability of two formulations[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=29) . Some BE-specific scenarios use two separate two-way crossovers or a single four-way crossover, but that is a bioequivalence recommendation rather than the general FE design[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=33) .


**Treatment conditions.** One period is fasted (empty stomach); the other is fed with the high-fat test meal[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=29) .


**Meal composition.** The FDA recommends a high-fat, high-calorie meal because it produces the greatest effect on GI physiology and systemic drug availability[15](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=15)[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=18)[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=22) . The meal is specified as roughly 50% of calories from fat and about 800 to 1000 kcal in the food-effect guidance[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=30) , and about 900 to 1000 kcal in the more recent immediate-release BE guidance[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=18)[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=22) . The target breakdown is approximately 150 kcal from protein, 250 kcal from carbohydrate, and 500 to 600 kcal from fat[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=30)[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=18)[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=22) . For some lower-risk products a lower-fat, lower-calorie meal may be acceptable, and if the reference/comparator labeling specifies a meal, that meal should be used[15](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=15)[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=18) .


**Timing of the meal and fasting.** In the fed arm, subjects begin the meal 30 minutes before dosing and finish it within 30 minutes, with the drug given 30 minutes after the meal starts[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=18)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=33) . Fasted studies are conducted after an overnight fast, with no food for at least 4 hours postdose[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=18)[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=40)[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=43) .


Reviews show these features in practice, frequently extending the design to a third arm to capture a low-fat meal. Deferasirox (Jadenu) used a single-center, open-label, randomized, three-period, six-sequence crossover comparing fasted, low-fat meal, and high-fat meal after a single dose[112](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=112) . Abiraterone acetate (Zytiga) used a Phase 1, single-dose, open-label, three-period crossover across fasting, low-fat, and high-fat meals[125](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=125) . Dexlansoprazole ODT (Dexilant SoluTab) used an open-label, randomized, single-dose, three-period crossover under high-fat conditions[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=117) . Eltrombopag (Promacta) used a Phase 1, open-label, randomized, three-period balanced crossover of fasted versus high-fat breakfast[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=119) .


### When a food-effect study can be waived


The clearest waiver pathway is for BCS Class 1 immediate-release products with high bioavailability. The FDA may waive an FE study for BCS Class 1 immediate-release drug products that also have high bioavailability (F greater than or equal to 0.85), and sponsors are advised to consult the agency on feasibility[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=34) .


The Biopharmaceutics Classification System also predicts where food effects are likely. For BCS Class I, food effects are least likely because absorption is generally pH- and site-independent; the FDA notes that more than 80% of BCS Class 1 immediate-release products are not affected by high-fat meals[15](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=15)[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=34) . For BCS Classes II, III, and IV, food effects are most likely and their direction and magnitude are difficult or impossible to predict without a fed study[15](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=15) . For immediate-release products submitted under an ANDA, a fed BE study is generally recommended except when both test and reference products are rapidly dissolving, have similar dissolution profiles, and are BCS Class I[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=14) . A food-effect study may also be unnecessary where a biowaiver is accepted for a formulation change[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=29) .


### Modified-release and extended-release products


For modified-release (MR) and extended-release (ER) products, food-effect studies serve a second purpose beyond exposure: they test whether the product maintains its intended release behavior or whether food triggers rapid release or "dose dumping." Reviews used the food-effect result to decide (1) whether the product genuinely behaved as modified-release, (2) whether food caused dose dumping or a clinically important exposure change, and (3) what the label should say about meals[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=87)[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=91)[95](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=95)[97](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=97)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=102)[106](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=106)[110](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=110)[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=111) .


Examples across the spectrum:


- **No meaningful effect, label "with or without food."** Diltiazem ER (Cardizem LA) showed small fed changes with 90% CIs within no-food-effect limits, and the reviewer concluded the label should state diltiazem can be administered with or without food[95](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=95) . Desvenlafaxine ER was found administrable without regard to meals, with labeling stating the food-effect changes were not expected to be clinically significant[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=98)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=102)[104](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=104) .
- **Food present but tolerated in labeling.** For desvenlafaxine fumarate ER, fed-state AUC rose about 29% (a reviewer comment later cited 37%) but the change was still judged not clinically significant, supporting "without regard to meals"[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=102)[104](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=104) .
- **Food altered release, label toward fasting or warnings.** Azithromycin ER (Zmax) showed faster release with food that negated the ER formulation's GI-tolerability advantage, so the review concluded it should be taken on an empty stomach[97](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=97) . Oxcarbazepine ER (Oxtellar XR) showed a significant increase in parent-drug peak exposure with food and was directed to be administered under fasting conditions[106](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=106) . Fluvastatin MR (Lescol) reviewers declined to allow "slow release" labeling and required that the large fed-state exposure increase and high variability be noted[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=91) . Hydrocodone ER (Hysingla ER) had a definitive food-effect study showing higher fed Cmax and AUC, and the review framed food as materially changing PK[100](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=100) .
- **Dose-dumping and alcohol testing.** MR oral products commonly triggered in vitro alcohol dose-dumping studies. Deutetrabenazine XR (Austedo XR) reported no in vitro alcohol dose-dumping potential[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=87) . Sitagliptin/metformin XR (Zituvimet XR) showed lower release at 5%, 20%, and 40% alcohol and was judged to carry no additional alcohol dose-dumping risk[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=93) . Clonidine ER was found not to dose dump in the presence of a high-fat meal, though in vitro data suggested alcohol could modify its release[110](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=110)[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=111) .


### How the result drives labeling


The direction and magnitude of the food effect, filtered through clinical relevance, determines the administration instruction. The precedents fall into three buckets.


**Take with food (or with a meal).** When food increases exposure, reduces variability, improves tolerability, or matches the conditions used in pivotal trials. Canagliflozin/metformin XR (Invokamet XR) is directed to be administered with a meal (specifically the morning meal); metformin AUClast rose about 72% fed while canagliflozin was minimally affected[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=115)[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=129) . Venlafaxine ER absorption was unaffected by a high-fat meal, but nausea was more frequent on an empty stomach, so it is recommended with food[124](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=124) . Lubiprostone (Amitiza) had a 55% fed-state Cmax decrease with unchanged AUC; because clinical relevance was unclear and pivotal trials dosed with food, the review supported labeling for administration with food[127](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=127) . Amoxicillin (Moxatag) had unchanged AUC but a fed Cmax reduction and delayed Tmax, and the sponsor recommended administration with food[130](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=130) .


**Take on an empty stomach (or before meals / at bedtime).** When food increases exposure to a degree that raises safety concerns, or reduces a peak that matters clinically. Efavirenz (Sustiva) fed-state exposure rose sharply (tablet AUC about 28% higher, Cmax about 79% higher), and the label directs dosing at bedtime on an empty stomach to reduce high concentrations and CNS effects[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=116)[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=118) . Eltrombopag (Promacta) fed AUC fell about 59% and Cmax about 65%, a clinically significant reduction supporting empty-stomach administration[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=119) . Abiraterone (Zytiga) showed a dramatic food effect (high-fat meal raised Cmax roughly 17-fold and AUC roughly 10-fold), driving very specific fasting instructions[125](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=125) . Dexlansoprazole ODT lost 38% of Cmax with food and was directed to be taken at least 30 minutes before a meal[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=117) .


**Take without regard to food.** When the food effect is small or not clinically significant. Azithromycin's two 250 mg tablets were not decreased by a high-fat meal (although one capsule formulation was food-affected)[113](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=113)[114](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=114) . Fingolimod (Gilenya) showed similar fed and fasted AUC and Cmax with no meal restriction needed[121](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=121) . Amlodipine/atorvastatin (Caduet) showed no meaningful effect on amlodipine and a modest atorvastatin reduction (Cmax about 32%, AUC about 11%) that did not drive a meal restriction[126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=126)[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=128) .


The through-line is consistent with the guidance: a high-fat, single-dose crossover generates the exposure comparison, and the label instruction follows from whether that fed-versus-fasted difference is clinically meaningful for safety, efficacy, or variability[8](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=8)[11](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=11) .


### Practical takeaways


- Plan the food-effect assessment as an early Phase 1 activity, and design the *definitive* study on the final to-be-marketed formulation, or build a defensible bridge to it before relying on the result[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=9)[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=14)[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=65)[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=68) .
- Default to the randomized, single-dose, two-period fed-versus-fasted crossover with the high-fat, high-calorie meal (about 50% fat, roughly 800 to 1000 kcal), adding a low-fat arm when a graded meal effect is informative[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=29)[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=30)[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=18) .
- For BCS Class 1 immediate-release products with high bioavailability, discuss a possible waiver with the FDA rather than assuming one[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=34) .
- For modified-release products, expect the food-effect study to be read alongside dose-dumping and alcohol-release data, and expect fasting or warning language if food accelerates release or sharply raises peak exposure[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=87)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=93)[97](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=97)[106](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-expects-food-effect-studies-timing-design?showSourceNumber=106) .
